cases.script: p="$(printf '(%.0s' $(seq 257))1$(printf ')%.0s' $(seq 257))"; jq -n "$p"; echo s=$?; p="$(printf '[%.0s' $(seq 1000))1$(printf ']%.0s' $(seq 1000))"; jq -nc "$p"; echo s=$?

jq: maximum nesting level exceeded: deeper nesting is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: bash-tool's limit: jaq parses, compiles and runs a program recursively on the stack the shell uses, so a program nested more than 256 levels deep (fewer inside nested shell calls) is refused before it runs; jq runs it

cases.name: parse: jq refuses evaluation that would recurse past the stack
cases.script: jq -n 'def f: if . > 0 then (. - 1 | f) + 1 else 0 end; 2000 | f'; echo s=$?; jq -n 'def f: if . > 0 then . - 1 | f else . end; 100000 | f'; echo s=$?

stderr.text: jq: maximum nesting level exceeded: deeper nesting is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: bash-tool's limit: jaq evaluates recursively on the stack the shell uses, so evaluation that would recurse past what it holds (a recursive definition that is not a tail call, here 2,000 levels deep) stops with a refusal; jq runs it. Tail calls do not recurse
